seeds: Rare-event calibrated inference for the marginal monotone probability of necessity.
Conditional score-cell likelihood-ratio inversion across Poisson and Gaussian information regimes.

symbols.name: \(\widetilde P_n\)
symbols.def: \(\widetilde P_n\) is a law of \(X_{i,n},A_{i,n},Y_{i,n}(0),Y_{i,n}(1)\) whose observed-data marginal is \(P_n\).

symbols.name: \(\psi_{t,n}\)
symbols.space: a real-valued function of an observed unit and a nuisance pair
symbols.def: \(\psi_{t,n}\) is the PN score indexed by \(t\in[0,1]\) and defined in def:pn-score.

symbols.name: \(\widehat e_{-k,n}\)
symbols.def: \(\widehat e_{-k,n}\) is the clipped off-fold propensity fit in def:clipped-learners.

symbols.name: \(\widehat m_{0,-k,n}\)
symbols.def: \(\widehat m_{0,-k,n}\) is the clipped control-only off-fold outcome fit in def:clipped-learners.

symbols.name: \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{LR,PN}}_{n,\alpha}\)
symbols.def: \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{LR,PN}}_{n,\alpha}\) is the PN likelihood-ratio inversion defined in def:score-cell-lr-inversion.

symbols.name: \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{LR,PS}}_{n,\alpha}\)
symbols.def: \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{LR,PS}}_{n,\alpha}\) is the treatment-and-outcome-swapped counterpart defined in def:ps-lr-inversion.

symbols.name: \(\mathcal H^\beta(L)\)
symbols.def: \(\mathcal H^\beta(L)\) is the isotropic Hölder ball of order \(\beta\) and radius \(L\).

symbols.name: \(\varepsilon\)
symbols.def: \(\varepsilon\) is the overlap and clipping constant.

symbols.name: \(\bar d\)
symbols.def: \(\bar d\) is the factual-event upper bound.

symbols.name: \(c_v\)
symbols.def: \(c_v\) is the normalized score-variance lower bound.

symbols.name: \(P^{\mathrm{LF}}_{n,t}\)
symbols.def: \(P^{\mathrm{LF}}_{n,t}\) is the observed marginal of def:least-favorable-law.

symbols.name: \(\widetilde P^{\mathrm{LF}}_{n,t}\)
symbols.def: \(\widetilde P^{\mathrm{LF}}_{n,t}\) is the full-data law in def:least-favorable-law.

symbols.name: \(h\)
symbols.def: \(h\) is a fixed separation constant in the two-point converse.

novel.justification: High-threshold climate attribution and restrictive medical case definitions can make the factual treated case rare.  The condition retains both bounded effective-count and diverging effective-count sequences.

standard.name: bounded covariate density for sieve least squares

novel.justification: It holds when a high-threshold factual risk is uniformly rare across retained covariate strata, as in pre-specified climate regions or stratified stroke cohorts.  It excludes rarity created only by an unobserved shrinking covariate cell.

For fixed-dimensional Hölder regressions, clipped spline learners attain the displayed polynomial rates, while the logarithmic transition scale leaves those rates intact.  This is a law-level compatibility restriction on nuisance difficulty and rare-event information, not a property of a fitted estimator.

It holds away from a scientifically distinct deterministic-attribution degeneracy, for example when avoidable outcomes occur with probability bounded away from zero on a nonvanishing fraction of factual cases.  It is required only for the interior Gaussian score limit.

definitions.name: fixed-fold clipped spline learners
definitions.construction: For each \(k\), estimate \(e_n\) by least-squares regression of \(A\) on \(X\) outside \(I_{k,n}\) over a tensor-product spline sieve of dimension \(\lceil n^{p/(2\beta_e+p)}\rceil\).  Estimate \(m_{0,n}\) by least-squares regression of \(Y\) on \(X\) using only observations with \(A=0\) outside \(I_{k,n}\), over dimension \(\lceil n^{p/(2\beta_0+p)}\rceil\).  Clip the first fit to \([\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\), clip the second fit to \([0,1]\), and denote the pair by \(\widehat\eta_{-k,n}\).

definitions.name: cross-fitted full score-cell experiment
definitions.construction: For \(i\in I_{k,n}\), set \(\widehat\psi_{i,n}(t)=\psi_{t,n}(O_{i,n};\widehat\eta_{-k,n})\) and retain \(\widehat{\mathbb N}_{n,t}=\sum_{i=1}^n\delta_{(A_{i,n},Y_{i,n},\widehat\psi_{i,n}(t))}\) with all four \((A,Y)\) cells and their marks.

definitions.name: rare-event monotone PN observed-law class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{PN}}=\{P_n:\exists\widetilde P_n\text{ with observed-data marginal }P_n\text{ satisfying ass:consistency, ass:ignorability, ass:monotonicity, ass:overlap, ass:rare-event, ass:covariate-design, ass:holder-nuisances, ass:rare-localization, and ass:rate-compatibility}\}\).

definitions.name: rare-event monotone PS observed-law class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{PS}}=\{P_n:\mathfrak T(P_n)\text{ admits a full-data extension satisfying ass:consistency, ass:ignorability, ass:monotonicity, ass:overlap, ass:rare-event, ass:covariate-design, ass:holder-nuisances, ass:rare-localization, and ass:rate-compatibility}\}\), where \(\mathfrak T(P_n)\) is the push-forward of \(P_n\) under \(\mathfrak T(x,a,y)=(x,1-a,1-y)\).

definitions.name: binary least-favorable PN law
definitions.construction: For \(t\in[0,1]\), let \(\widetilde P^{\mathrm{LF}}_{n,t}\) satisfy \(X\sim\operatorname{Unif}([0,1]^p)\), \(A\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\), and \((Y(0),Y(1))\perp(X,A)\), with \(\widetilde P^{\mathrm{LF}}_{n,t}\{Y(0)=0,Y(1)=1\}=2t d_n^{\mathrm{PN}}\), \(\widetilde P^{\mathrm{LF}}_{n,t}\{Y(0)=1,Y(1)=1\}=2(1-t)d_n^{\mathrm{PN}}\), and \(\widetilde P^{\mathrm{LF}}_{n,t}\{Y(0)=0,Y(1)=0\}=1-2d_n^{\mathrm{PN}}\).  Define \(P^{\mathrm{LF}}_{n,t}\) as its observed marginal under \(Y=Y(A)\).

definitions.name: randomized conditional score-cell likelihood-ratio inversion
definitions.construction: For each \(t\in[0,1]\), condition on every fold training sample, validation covariates, and the common-cell component of def:crossfit-score-cells.  Retain the score marks in all four \((A,Y)\) cells, model the remaining score-bearing indicators jointly by their conditional Poisson-binomial experiment, profile its cell intensities over \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{PN}}\), and compare its profile likelihood ratio with a randomized Neyman--Feldman--Cousins critical value from the least-favorable conditional law.  Include \(t\) when that randomized test does not reject; set \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{LR,PN}}_{n,\alpha}=[0,1]\) whenever \(\sum_{i=1}^nA_{i,n}Y_{i,n}=0\).

definitions.name: treatment-and-outcome-swapped PS likelihood-ratio inversion
definitions.construction: Apply def:score-cell-lr-inversion to the transformed observations \(\mathfrak T(O_{i,n})=(X_{i,n},1-A_{i,n},1-Y_{i,n})\), then map its PN parameter back to \(\vartheta_n\); call the output \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{LR,PS}}_{n,\alpha}\).

definitions.name: selected-event score-cell inversion handle
definitions.construction: Index def:score-cell-lr-inversion by an admissible threshold or projection class, condition jointly on its score-cell processes, and invert a least-favorable supremum likelihood-ratio statistic before selecting the event definition.

sampling_model.design: For each \(n\), observed units are independent with common law \(P_n\), the observed projection of a full-data law in the relevant monotone class.
sampling_model.units: Each unit supplies covariates \(X\), binary treatment \(A\), and binary outcome \(Y\).
sampling_model.treatment: Consistency, ignorability, monotonicity, and overlap identify the PN and PS functionals.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The propensity fit uses off-fold observations; the PN control regression is fitted only on off-fold control observations.  The PS construction is its treatment-and-outcome-swapped analogue.

statements.statement: Under ass:consistency, ass:ignorability, ass:monotonicity, and ass:overlap, \(\theta_n\) and \(\vartheta_n\) equal def:pn-functional and def:ps-functional, respectively, and \(E_{P_n}[\psi_{\theta_n,n}(O;\eta_n)]=0\).
statements.justification: It fixes both causal ratio targets and the PN test equation before rare-event calibration.
statements.gap: \citet{TianWu2025} supplies the regular PN and PS identification benchmark, not the conditional rare-event experiment.
statements.consumer: It supplies the parameter restrictions profiled by the PN and PS likelihood-ratio procedures.

statements.statement: Under ass:iid-row, ass:overlap, ass:covariate-design, ass:holder-nuisances, and ass:rare-localization, def:clipped-learners satisfies \(\max_{k\le K}\lVert\widehat e_{-k,n}-e_n\rVert_{L^2(P_{X,n})}=O_{P_n}(r_{e,n})\) and \(\max_{k\le K}\lVert\widehat m_{0,-k,n}-m_{0,n}\rVert_{L^2(\omega_nP_{X,n})}=O_{P_n}(r_{0,n})\).  Since \(\kappa_n=\log n\), \(\sqrt{\kappa_n}r_{e,n}\to0\) and \(\sqrt{\kappa_n}r_{0,n}\to0\).
statements.justification: It certifies the fixed-fold propensity and control-only outcome fits used in the score-cell experiment.
statements.gap: Regular DML theory does not derive this rare-local weighted control-regression rate for the PN ratio score.
statements.consumer: It bounds the conditional intensity drift induced by cross-fitting.

statements.statement: Under ass:monotonicity and ass:overlap, the oracle and clipped cross-fitted PN score marks have a uniform envelope, and their score-bearing rare-cell conditional variances are bounded above by \(C_\varepsilon d_n^{\mathrm{PN}}\) for a finite constant depending only on overlap.  The treatment-and-outcome swap gives the same assertion on \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{PS}}\).
statements.justification: A rare-scale envelope and variance bound permit conditional Poisson-binomial calibration before Gaussian approximation is available.
statements.gap: Rare-binomial interval analyses such as \citet{McGrathBurke2024} do not contain learned orthogonal causal score marks.
statements.consumer: It supplies the finite-information control used in thm:lr-frontier.

statements.statement: If \(c_X\le1\le C_X\), \(\varepsilon\le1/2\le1-\varepsilon\), \(C_\omega\ge1\), \(2\bar d\le1\), and the Hölder radii contain \(e_n\equiv1/2\) and \(m_{0,n}\equiv2(1-t)d_n^{\mathrm{PN}}\), then, for every \(t\in[0,1]\), \(P^{\mathrm{LF}}_{n,t}\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{PN}}\), \(\theta_n=t\), and its factual-event probability is \(d_n^{\mathrm{PN}}\).
statements.justification: It certifies rather than assumes membership of the explicit bounded causal submodel.
statements.gap: Generic ratio converses do not verify a monotone causal PN least-favorable law with the declared smoothness and localization conditions.
statements.consumer: It transfers the two-point converse to every procedure honest over the declared PN class.

statements.statement: Under ass:iid-row, ass:consistency, ass:ignorability, ass:monotonicity, ass:overlap, ass:rare-event, ass:covariate-design, ass:holder-nuisances, ass:rare-localization, and ass:rate-compatibility, the randomized inversion in def:score-cell-lr-inversion satisfies, for every fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\), \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{PN}}}P_n\{\theta_n\in\mathcal C^{\mathrm{LR,PN}}_{n,\alpha}\}\ge1-\alpha\) and \(\limsup_{n\to\infty}\sup_{P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{PN}}}\frac{E_{P_n}[\operatorname{diam}(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{LR,PN}}_{n,\alpha})]}{\min\{1,[n d_n^{\mathrm{PN}}]^{-1/2}\}}\le C_\alpha<\infty\).  The treatment-and-outcome-swapped inversion satisfies the same two assertions with \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{PS}},\vartheta_n,\mathcal C^{\mathrm{LR,PS}}_{n,\alpha},d_n^{\mathrm{PS}}\) in place of their PN counterparts.
statements.justification: It gives one randomized conditional procedure whose coverage and expected diameter are honest from zero factual counts through the Gaussian regime.
statements.gap: \citet{TianWu2025} gives fixed-law efficient PN and PS inference, whereas this theorem treats triangular arrays with a factual-event probability that can leave only a bounded number of score-bearing observations.
statements.consumer: It produces valid rare-event attribution sets for climate and stroke applications while quantifying the attainable precision.

statements.statement: Under the assumptions of thm:lr-frontier and ass:score-nondegeneracy, if \(n d_n^{\mathrm{PN}}\to\infty\), then the conditional profile likelihood-ratio experiment in def:score-cell-lr-inversion is locally asymptotically normal, its Gaussian likelihood-ratio recovery has influence function \((d_n^{\mathrm{PN}})^{-1}\psi_{\theta_n,n}(O;\eta_n)\), and that influence function equals Tian and Wu's monotone-PN efficient influence function.  When \(\inf_n d_n^{\mathrm{PN}}>0\), this is their regular Gaussian limit; the transformed statement holds for PS.
statements.justification: It derives the Gaussian endpoint from the conditional likelihood experiment rather than assuming a central limit theorem.
statements.gap: The monotonicity EIF and asymptotic-normality result in \citet{TianWu2025}, Section 3, is a fixed-law regular benchmark and does not cover a diverging score norm as \(d_n^{\mathrm{PN}}\) vanishes.
statements.consumer: It permits standard efficient likelihood-ratio reporting once the expected factual count diverges.

statements.statement: Let \(D_n\) be measurable random subsets of \([0,1]\) with \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{PN}}}P_n\{\theta_n\in D_n\}\ge1-\alpha\).  There are \(c_\alpha>0\) and, for each such procedure, \(n_0(D)\) such that for all \(n\ge n_0(D)\), \(\sup_{t\in[0,1]}E_{P^{\mathrm{LF}}_{n,t}}[\operatorname{diam}(D_n)]\ge c_\alpha\min\{1,[n d_n^{\mathrm{PN}}]^{-1/2}\}\).  Equivalently, every uniformly honest measurable procedure obeys \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}\sup_{P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{PN}}}\frac{E_{P_n}[\operatorname{diam}(D_n)]}{\min\{1,[n d_n^{\mathrm{PN}}]^{-1/2}\}}\ge c_\alpha\).  For fixed sufficiently small \(h>0\), the two submodel laws at \(t=1/2\pm h\min\{1,[n d_n^{\mathrm{PN}}]^{-1/2}\}\) satisfy a product Kullback--Leibler bound at most \(16h^2\), hence have uniformly bounded total variation.  Applying \(\mathfrak T\) gives the same converse for PS.
statements.justification: It supplies the matching information-theoretic side for measurable procedures, with the eventual-\(n\) quantifier required by an asymptotic coverage premise.
statements.gap: \citet{GleserHwang1987} gives a general ratio impossibility and \citet{CaiGuo2017} supplies expected-length methodology, but neither yields this bounded monotone-PN rate on a certified causal submodel.
statements.consumer: Together with thm:lr-frontier, it shows that rare factual information creates an unavoidable precision frontier.

statements.statement: Under \(P^{\mathrm{LF}}_{n,t}\), if \(n d_n^{\mathrm{PN}}\to\lambda<\infty\), then the rare counts \(N_{11,n}=\sum_{i=1}^n1\{A_{i,n}=1,Y_{i,n}=1\}\) and \(N_{01,n}=\sum_{i=1}^n1\{A_{i,n}=0,Y_{i,n}=1\}\) converge jointly to independent variables \(Z_1\sim\operatorname{Poisson}(\lambda)\) and \(Z_0\sim\operatorname{Poisson}(\lambda(1-t))\), while the common-cell counts have centered Gaussian limits.  The conditional likelihood-ratio experiment in thm:lr-frontier converges to the corresponding marked-Poisson likelihood-ratio experiment; thm:diameter-lower therefore gives nonshrinking worst-case expected diameter in this regime.
statements.justification: It identifies the actual finite-information boundary rather than applying a Gaussian approximation to sparse cells.
statements.gap: \citet{Huwang1995} establishes nonuniform normal-approximation coverage for binomial intervals; the result here is a marked causal score-cell boundary experiment.
statements.consumer: It tells attribution analysts when a wide confidence set is information-theoretically appropriate.

statements.statement: Can the simultaneous score-cell inversion in def:selection-handle retain the coverage and diameter order of thm:lr-frontier after a climate threshold or multivariate projection is selected to maximize causal evidence?
statements.justification: Extreme-event attribution commonly chooses the event definition, changing both the target and its effective count.
statements.gap: \citet{HannartNaveau2018} and \citet{KirilioukNaveau2020} optimize causal evidence under extreme-value models but do not give a selection-honest learned score-cell confidence set.
statements.consumer: It would permit uncertainty statements for selected climate attribution events.

tldr: The proposal studies point-identified probabilities of necessity and sufficiency when the relevant factual conditioning event is rare.  A randomized Feldman--Cousins/Neyman profile likelihood-ratio inversion conditions on cross-fitting training samples, validation covariates, and common cells, then retains the full marked four-cell score experiment.  It is designed to give uniform coverage and the sharp expected-diameter order \(\min\{1,(n d_n)^{-1/2}\}\), with a nonshrinking marked-Poisson boundary and Tian--Wu efficient Gaussian recovery.  A certified two-point monotone causal submodel supplies the matching converse; selection-honest event definitions remain open.

project_justification.gap: Existing PN and PS inference is regular-law theory.  Tian and Wu derive monotone efficient influence functions and regular asymptotic inference, but do not analyze a factual conditioning event whose information count can remain bounded.
project_justification.niche: The factual-event probability indexes a single conditional experiment that transitions from a discrete marked-Poisson likelihood to a semiparametric Gaussian likelihood.
project_justification.fill: The project formulates randomized full score-cell likelihood-ratio inversion, proves its uniform coverage and sharp diameter frontier, recovers the regular efficient benchmark, and matches it with a bounded causal two-point converse.

related_work: \citet{TianWu2025}, Section 3, derives monotonicity-based PN and PS influence functions and regular asymptotic-normality theory.  thm:conditional-lan is a strict triangular-array tightening: it reduces to that benchmark under strict overlap and a fixed positive factual-event probability, but treats the Poisson-to-Gaussian transition when the factual probability vanishes.  \citet{CuellarKennedy2020}, Section 3, studies regular influence-function inference for a projection of a covariate-indexed probability of causation; it informs the score construction but does not target this marginal rare-count ratio.  \citet{ZhangWangMiao2025} studies efficient confidence intervals for generally partially identified PN bounds without monotonicity; it is a distinct target and is not a frontier comparator.  \citet{ChernozhukovEtAl2018DML} and \citet{Chen2007} provide the fixed-fold orthogonalization and spline-rate ingredients.  \citet{Huwang1995} supplies the nonuniform normal-approximation failure motivating discrete calibration, whereas \citet{McGrathBurke2024} motivates rare-binomial coverage and relative-margin comparisons.  \citet{MikushevaSun2022} motivates least-favorable test inversion under weak information.  \citet{GleserHwang1987}, \citet{KhanTamer2010}, and \citet{CaiGuo2017} motivate honest-diameter converses.  \citet{HannartNaveau2018} supplies the climate consumer and the stroke application in \citet{TianWu2025} supplies the medical consumer.
honest_scope: The converse is a lower bound for any measurable procedure honest over a class containing the certified covariate-homogeneous submodel.  When the factual probability is bounded away from zero, thm:conditional-lan reduces to Tian and Wu's regular efficient limit.  Selection-honest inference over data-adaptive climate event definitions remains open.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Under regular laws, monotonicity identifies PN and PS and efficient influence-function estimators have regular asymptotic normal limits.
Section 3 gives regular influence-function inference for a projection of a covariate-indexed probability of causation.
Efficient confidence intervals are developed for generally partially identified PN bounds without monotonicity.
Cross-fitting with Neyman-orthogonal scores gives regular root-\(n\) inference under nuisance-rate conditions.
Test inversion gives weak-information-robust inference in many-instrument models.
Rare-binomial intervals are compared by coverage and relative margin of error.
Ratio-like zero-information models can preclude confidence sets with finite expected diameter.
